title: taste-check config
description: Checks are driven entirely by this file. The tool ships no palette, no class list and no contrast floors.

contrast.description: WCAG contrast ratios computed from your own custom properties.

tokens.description: CSS files holding the custom properties. Paths resolve against this config file. Later files override earlier ones.

themes.description: Each theme is an ordered list of scopes. Later scopes win, which is the cascade for equal specificity. There is no specificity resolution.

oneOf.description: A selector, matched exactly against one entry in a rule's selector list.

atRule.description: Opt into declarations nested in a matching at-rule prelude, for example "prefers-color-scheme: dark". Conditional at-rules (@media, @supports, @container, @scope) are ignored without this. Grouping at-rules like @layer are always transparent, so you only name one to narrow a scope to it.

pairs.description: What must clear what. A pair naming a token that does not exist is a failure, never a skip.

fg.description: A token name like --text, or a literal colour.

bg.description: As fg, but it must resolve to an opaque colour.

min.description: The floor this pair must clear. No default: you decide what the rule is.

label.description: Why this pair matters. Printed with the result.

themes.description: Limit the pair to these themes. Omit to check it in all of them.

treatments.description: Class names and literal values in markup, against a list you supply.

files.description: Markup to scan. A pattern matching nothing is a failure, never a clean run.

elements.description: Element names to scan. Use ["*"] or omit for every element.

approvedClasses.description: Every class name allowed to appear. Anything else is reported.

allowPrefixes.description: Class name prefixes that are always allowed, for a deliberate escape hatch.

approvedValues.description: Literal values allowed in inline styles. Everything else that looks like a colour or a length is reported.

judge.description: A fresh-eyes review of your screenshots against your checklist, run by a model command you supply. Run with `taste-check judge`. Verdicts are advisory unless failOn says otherwise.

checklist.description: A file of checklist lines. List items ("- ..." or "1. ...") are what gets judged; everything else is treated as prose. taste-check ships no checklist.

shots.description: Screenshots to hand the judge. Matching nothing is a failure: a judge with nothing to look at cannot fail, so it does not get to pass.

shotCommand.description: Optional command run before the judge to produce the screenshots. Runs from this config file's directory.

command.description: The model command. It receives the prompt on stdin and the image paths as arguments, and must reply with the documented JSON. Runs from this config file's directory.

failOn.description: Whether a "fail" verdict affects the exit code. Defaults to never: a model's verdict is not reproducible, so it does not gate a build unless you decide it should. Independent of this, a judge that could not run always exits 1.
